source: LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA discovery papers (arXiv abstracts); values verified against each abstract by scripts/build-gw-events.mjs

events.name: GW150914
events.about: The first gravitational waves ever detected.

events.name: GW151226
events.about: The second detection: lighter, spinning black holes.

events.name: GW170104
events.about: A 50-solar-mass merger nearly 3 billion light-years away.

events.name: GW170814
events.about: The first detection by three detectors (LIGO and Virgo).

events.name: GW170817
events.about: Two neutron stars: the first merger also seen in light (a kilonova in NGC 4993).
events.massNote: The abstract gives a total of 2.74 M☉ and a component range of 1.17–1.60 M☉; the split 1.46 + 1.27 is chosen within that range.

events.name: GW190425
events.about: The heaviest binary neutron star system known.
events.massNote: The abstract gives a total of 3.4 M☉ and a low-spin component range of 1.45–1.88 M☉; the split 1.75 + 1.65 is chosen within that range.

events.name: GW190521
events.about: The most massive merger: the remnant is an intermediate-mass black hole.

events.name: GW190814
events.about: A very lopsided pair: the 2.6 M☉ partner is the lightest black hole or the heaviest neutron star known.
events.massNote: The abstract gives 90% ranges of 22.2–24.3 and 2.50–2.67 M☉ (its title says 23 and 2.6).

events.name: GW200105
events.about: One of the first neutron star–black hole mergers.

events.name: GW200115
events.about: A neutron star swallowed by a black hole.

events.name: GW230529
events.about: A partner in the "mass gap" between the heaviest neutron stars and the lightest black holes.
events.massNote: Masses are the midpoints of the 90% ranges in the abstract (2.5–4.5 and 1.2–2.0 M☉).
